purpose: Freeze the prospective 2027-2028 Minnesota member-history cap-20 shadow validation before any in-scope outcomes exist. The candidate remains non-serving and may not change production probabilities from this plan alone.

retrospectiveSummary.interpretation: Cap 20 remained a plausible shadow candidate because Brier, ECE, accuracy, and chamber expected-Yes error improved on the already-revealed exact holdout, but log loss and absolute signed residual worsened. Those weaknesses motivate stricter prospective guards and do not justify a runtime change.

prospectiveCohort.forecastSelection: For each resolved in-scope vote event, use the latest otherwise-eligible Quick forecast revision whose generated calendar date is strictly earlier than the official vote date. Same-day revisions are excluded because event ordering cannot be proved from a date-only vote timestamp.
prospectiveCohort.enrollmentRule: Enroll every forecast revision generated by the production Quick runtime in the 2027-2028 session for House or Senate when both uncapped serving probabilities and cap-20 shadow probabilities were persisted before the outcome. Outcome, later vote margin, bill result, mechanic presence, or candidate performance may not affect enrollment or revision selection.

revealPolicy.notes: Do not compute comparative candidate-versus-baseline outcome metrics for the prospective cohort before the reveal timestamp. Routine production resolution may continue, but the cap experiment may not inspect aggregate outcome deltas early.

primaryHouseDecisionRule.interpretation: A prospective House pass requires a non-trivial Brier improvement under both member-weighted and equal-case estimands, no ECE or absolute signed-bias regression, no chamber expected-Yes MAE regression, and tightly bounded log-loss/accuracy tradeoffs.

senateSafetyRule.ifMinimumNotMet: Global promotion is blocked. A House-only result may motivate a separately frozen chamber-specific follow-up but cannot change the global member model.

required: member-weighted Brier, log loss, accuracy, ECE, and signed residual
